findings.body: `resize` changed from `(src, w)` to `(src, filter, w)`. Existing callers that still pass `(src, w)` will treat the numeric width as `filter` and leave `w` as `undefined`, producing a broken `-resize undefinedx` invocation (and, with the new `exec` path, odd shell expansion). If this is a published helper, bump the major version or give `filter` a default and keep width as the second argument.

summary:
## Verdict

Critical command-injection regression in `resize`: user-controlled path and filter strings are passed through a shell.

## Narrative

`src/images/resize.ts` switched from `execFile` (argv array, no shell) to `exec` with a template string. Both `src` and `filter` are interpolated into that string; the new comment even frames `filter` as user-composed. Any value such as a crafted `src` with `"; …` or a `filter` with `; curl … | sh` runs as shell metacharacters on the host.

ImageMagick's `-filter` takes a single filter name token (e.g. `Lanczos`, `Mitchell`). It does not require a shell. Keep `execFile` and pass `-filter` plus a validated allowlisted name as separate argv elements.

The function signature also gained a middle `filter` parameter (`(src, w)` to `(src, filter, w)`), which is a breaking call-site change for any external consumer of this export.

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: The patch replaces safe execFile argv passing with exec and interpolates untrusted `src` and `filter` into a shell command string; `filter` is unquoted and the comment calls it user-composed, so shell metacharacters yield host command execution. Critical severity is appropriate for RCE.
